author: reek
body: Different agents for different modes. The dev console agent understands compiler internals and build commands. The UI agent understands layout, widgets, and user interaction. Each can be a different model or the same model with different system prompts.

author: reek
body: The last two existed as labels and as menu items and as nothing else. `role-switch-menu` has offered "Code Reviewer" and "General Assistant" since it was written, and neither had a RoleConfig to switch to, so two of its five entries could only ever be refusals. A menu that offers what the code cannot supply is the same defect as an effect with no handler, caught later.

author: reek
body: Named for its type, because `AgentRuntime` also defines `role-label` and over a different sum: its one labels who spoke in a chat, this one which job the agent is doing. Both were called `role-label`, so a chapter that cited both got whichever the resolver reached first, which is a CDX3006 the compiler has been warning about. `raft-role-label` and `member-role-label` elsewhere in the tree are the same convention.
